citation: Bansal G, Nushi B, Kamar E, Weld DS, Lasecki WS, Horvitz E. Updates in Human-AI Teams: Understanding and Addressing the Performance/Compatibility Tradeoff.
venue_and_status: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence 33(01):2429-2437; published (AAAI OJS PDF read)
problem: Updates that raise an AI system's accuracy can break the user's learned mental model of when to trust it.
method: Defines locally and globally compatible updates and the compatibility score C(h1,h2)=sum_x A(x,h1(x))*A(x,h2(x)) / sum_x A(x,h1(x)) (Eq. 1; A = whether the recommended action is correct); dissonance-penalised retraining loss L_c = L + lambda_c*D; CAJA user-study platform.
data: MTurk user studies on CAJA; recidivism, in-hospital mortality (MIMIC-III) and credit-risk datasets; logistic regression and MLP.
main_result: Accuracy-improving but incompatible updates lowered human-AI team performance; with h1 trained on 200 and h2 on 5000 examples, compatibility was as low as 40% (logistic regression, in-hospital mortality); the dissonance loss gives an explorable performance/compatibility trade-off.
relevance: Primary source of the compatibility score that Srivastava et al. later named backward trust compatibility (BTC); earliest formal definition of update compatibility found in this search.
not_established: Classification/actions only; single timepoint; no continuous outputs or measurements.
code_or_data: CAJA platform described; no repository checked

citation: Srivastava M, Nushi B, Kamar E, Shah S, Horvitz E. An Empirical Analysis of Backward Compatibility in Machine Learning Systems.
venue_and_status: Proceedings of the 26th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery & Data Mining (KDD 2020), pp. 3272-3280; published; arXiv:2008.04572v1 read (camera-ready not compared)
problem: Model updates in multi-component ML systems introduce new errors that downstream components are not prepared for.
method: Defines BTC = sum_i 1[h1(x_i)=y_i, h2(x_i)=y_i] / sum_i 1[h1(x_i)=y_i] (Eq. 1; stated to match Bansal's compatibility score) and BEC = sum_i 1[h1(x_i)!=y_i, h2(x_i)!=y_i] / sum_i 1[h2(x_i)!=y_i] (Eq. 2); label, feature and outlier noise experiments; dissonance regularisation; OCR pipeline case study.
data: FICO credit (logistic regression), MNIST (3-layer CNN), CIFAR-10 (ResNet-18), IMDB (BERT), Chars74K OCR pipeline.
main_result: Incompatibility arises even with identical training data (25 logistic-regression trials on FICO: BTC 94.5 +/- 1.31%, BEC 78.3 +/- 2.15%) and grows with biased noise although overall accuracy gains stay positive.
relevance: Primary source of the names BTC and BEC and their exact definitions; same-data retraining is already incompatible, paralleling the paper's continued-training control.
not_established: Classification only; no continuous outputs, measurements or change over time.
code_or_data: Microsoft BackwardCompatibilityML library (github.com/microsoft/BackwardCompatibilityML; documentation checked, classifiers only)

citation: Shen Y, Xiong Y, Xia W, Soatto S. Towards Backward-Compatible Representation Learning.
venue_and_status: 2020 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR), pp. 6367-6376; published; arXiv:2003.11942v3 read
problem: New embedding models normally force 'backfilling' (re-processing every stored gallery image) because new features cannot be compared with stored old features.
method: Strict criterion d(phi_new(x_i),phi_old(x_j)) >= d(phi_old(x_i),phi_old(x_j)) for different classes and <= for the same class (Eq. 1); empirical compatibility criterion M(phi_new,phi_old;Q,D) > M(phi_old,phi_old;Q,D) (Eq. 2); update gain G = [M(new,old) - M(old,old)] / [M(new*,new*) - M(old,old)] with the best backfilled new model as paragon (Eq. 9); influence loss (backward-compatible training, BCT).
data: Face recognition: IMDBFace training data; IJB-C 1:N search and 1:1 verification.
main_result: Independently trained old and new models give near-0% cross-model accuracy and l2 regularisation does not fix it; basic BCT satisfies the empirical criterion with update gains of 26.26% (1:1 verification) and 44.98% (1:N search); variants using the added training classes reach 27.25-30.00% on 1:1 verification.
relevance: Closest structural template for a longitudinal compatibility criterion: a cross-version comparison (new query vs stored old gallery) is judged against same-version comparisons and normalised by the reprocessed (backfilled) paragon; backfilling corresponds to the paper's reprocessing.
not_established: Retrieval embeddings and accuracy, not measurements; no change over time.

citation: Träuble F, von Kügelgen J, Kleindessner M, Locatello F, Schölkopf B, Gehler P. Backward-Compatible Prediction Updates: A Probabilistic Approach.
venue_and_status: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 34 (NeurIPS 2021), pp. 116-128; published (official proceedings PDF; main paper read, appendix not read)
problem: When a better model becomes available, which stored predictions on a large unlabelled dataset should be re-evaluated, and should they be replaced (the Prediction Update Problem)?
method: Bayesian posterior over true labels combining all model predictions; entropy-based selection under a re-evaluation budget; update rules (MB, MBME, cost ratio); baselines Replace (always overwrite, 'a.k.a. backfilling') and majority vote; metrics accuracy, NF, NFR = sum NF/(N*T), PF/NF and BTC/BEC (formal definitions in Appendix A.2, not read).
data: ImageNet, ObjectNet and CIFAR-10 validation sets; 17 torchvision models used as a sequence of updates.
main_result: Probabilistic update strategies retain accuracy gains with far fewer negative flips than always replacing stored predictions, across budgets.
relevance: Closest ML analogue of the paper's question: keep stored outputs of the old model or reprocess (backfill) them with the new one.
not_established: Class labels only; no continuous measurements; no paired timepoints or change.

citation: Milani Fard M, Cormier Q, Canini K, Gupta M. Launch and Iterate: Reducing Prediction Churn.
venue_and_status: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 29 (NIPS 2016); published (official proceedings PDF; official BibTeX has no page numbers)
problem: Successive retraining changes many predictions neutrally (unnecessary churn), which hampers testing and usability.
method: Churn between two binary classifiers C(f1,f2) = E_(X,Y)~D[1{f1(X)*f2(X) < 0}] (Eq. 1), i.e. the expected fraction of test examples with differing predictions; smooth churn relaxation; MCMC stabilisation operator that regularises a new classifier towards the previous one; stability-based bounds.
data: Three UCI benchmark datasets; ridge, random-forest and SVM regressors thresholded as classifiers.
main_result: Stabilisation reduces churn without adversely affecting accuracy; churn bounded through algorithmic stability.
relevance: Primary definition of prediction churn between consecutive model versions; predates the backward-compatibility papers.
not_established: Binary classification only; no measurements or longitudinal comparison.

citation: Pianykh OS, Langs G, Dewey M, Enzmann DR, Herold CJ, Schoenberg SO, Brink JA. Continuous Learning AI in Radiology: Implementation Principles and Early Applications.
venue_and_status: Radiology 297(1):6-14; published (special report); abstract only, full text paywalled
problem: Static radiology AI models do not adapt to changing data and environments.
method: Narrative report on concepts and requirements for continuous-learning AI, with examples from emerging applications.
data: Not applicable.
main_result: Argues that radiology AI must move beyond replicating static models towards continuous learning and sets out implementation principles (abstract).
relevance: Radiology anchor for continuous model updating (Introduction context).
not_established: Abstract-level reading only; the abstract does not address measurement consistency across versions.

citation: Feng J, Phillips RV, Malenica I, Bishara A, Hubbard AE, Celi LA, Pirracchio R. Clinical artificial intelligence quality improvement: towards continual monitoring and updating of AI algorithms in healthcare.
venue_and_status: npj Digital Medicine 5:66; published (perspective); open access, read in full (PMC9156743)
problem: Deployed clinical AI degrades under dataset shift and needs continual monitoring and updating.
method: Perspective proposing hospital AI quality-improvement (AI-QI) units; statistical process control for monitoring; update types ordered by complexity (recalibration of continuous scores, model revision, full retraining); reactive vs continual updating; meta-procedures and online hypothesis testing to approve modifications.
data: Hypothetical hypotension early-warning example; literature.
main_result: Procedures for continual model updating are still nascent; simple updates such as recalibration can be effective; approved modifications need performance guarantees.
relevance: Context for monitoring and updating clinical AI; recalibration as the simplest update relates to the paper's scalar cross-calibration maps.
not_established: Does not address consistency of outputs across versions or longitudinal measurements.

citation: Vokinger KN, Feuerriegel S, Kesselheim AS. Continual learning in medical devices: FDA's action plan and beyond.
venue_and_status: The Lancet Digital Health 3(6):e337-e338; published comment; publisher page returned HTTP 403, first paragraph read via OpenAlex
problem: Regulating locked versus adaptive (continual-learning) AI/ML medical software.
method: Comment on the FDA action plan for AI/ML-based software as a medical device.
data: Not applicable.
main_result: Distinguishes locked algorithms from adaptive ones whose decision logic is updated with new data while retaining previous knowledge (first paragraph).
relevance: Regulatory framing of continual learning in devices (overlaps T6).
not_established: Content beyond the first paragraph not verified.

citation: Xie Y, Lai Y-A, Xiong Y, Zhang Y, Soatto S. Regression Bugs Are In Your Model! Measuring, Reducing and Analyzing Regressions In NLP Model Updates.
venue_and_status: Proceedings of ACL-IJCNLP 2021 (Volume 1: Long Papers), pp. 6589-6602; published (ACL Anthology PDF read)
problem: Regressions (negative flips) when updating NLP classifiers.
method: R_NF(D_reg,f_old,f_new) = |{x: f_old(x)=y, f_new(x)!=y}| / |D_reg| on a regression set, by analogy with software regression testing (following Yan et al.); constrained optimisation relaxed to distillation; ensembles; CheckList behavioural tests; KL divergence of predicted probabilities and l2 distance of representations proposed as continuous proxies for training.
data: GLUE tasks; updates among BERT, RoBERTa, ELECTRA and ALBERT models.
main_result: Regression is prevalent (at least 1.98% R_NF across tasks and settings while mean accuracy gain was 1.4%); changing only the random seed gave up to 3.56% negative flips; distillation and ensembles reduce R_NF.
relevance: Regression-testing framing of update compatibility; seed-only retraining already causes regressions.
not_established: Classification only; the continuous quantities are training penalties, not compatibility metrics.

citation: Fontaine J, Suszko M, di Franco F, Leroux A, Bonnet E, Bosset M, Langrand-Escure J, Clippe S, Fleury B, Guy J-B. Robustness evaluation of an artificial intelligence-based automatic contouring software in daily routine practice.
venue_and_status: Physica Medica 137:105065; published; abstract
problem: How commercial software updates and image quality affect AI auto-contouring accuracy.
method: Software-update cohort contoured by six versions of Limbus AI; volumetric Dice and HD95 against reference contours; image-quality cohort with reconstruction, noise and resolution degradations.
data: 40 CT scans (20 thorax, 10 pelvis, 10 head and neck) for versions; 20 patients x 12 reconstructions for image quality.
main_result: Dice improved across versions for re-trained structures (breast contour Dice fell 1% between v1.5 and v1.8B3, not significant); noise and resolution degradation reduced performance.
relevance: Clinical example of version-to-version evaluation of a commercial segmenter by single-timepoint overlap (competitor check; overlaps T2).
not_established: No between-version volume agreement, no longitudinal change, no mixed-version comparison.

citation: Sakai T. A Generalized Backward Compatibility Metric.
venue_and_status: Proceedings of the 28th ACM SIGKDD Conference (KDD 2022), pp. 1525-1535; published; abstract only (ACM DL blocked automated access; no open copy found)
problem: Backward-compatibility metrics lack a common theoretical basis and behave poorly for imbalanced classes.
method: Shows existing metrics assess essentially the same quantity; proposes a generalised backward compatibility (GBC) metric representing them; estimation-error bound; variant for imbalanced classification.
data: Not verified.
main_result: Existing backward-compatibility metrics are special cases of GBC and are unsuitable for imbalanced classification (abstract).
relevance: Unifying reference for the classification compatibility-metric family.
not_established: Exact GBC definition not read; classification only.

citation: Wu R, Guo C, Hannun A, van der Maaten L. Fixes That Fail: Self-Defeating Improvements in Machine-Learning Systems.
venue_and_status: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 34 (NeurIPS 2021), pp. 11745-11756; published (official PDF; definitions and setup read)
problem: Can improving one model in a multi-model system make the system worse?
method: Systems as directed acyclic graphs of models; Definition 2.1 (self-defeating improvement: replacing v by v' lowers v's test loss but raises the loss of at least one downstream model even after all downstream models are retrained); Bayes error decompositions; stereo-based car and pedestrian detection experiment.
data: Illustrative systems and a stereo-based detection system.
main_result: Improving an upstream model can deteriorate downstream models even after retraining, because of entanglement.
relevance: Formalises that a component's own improvement need not improve the system output (cf. a Dice gain without measurement compatibility).
not_established: No stored outputs or longitudinal measurements; downstream models are retrained, unlike a fixed subtraction of stored values.

citation: Cao H, Morotti A, Mazzacane F, Desser D, Schlunk F, Güttler C, Kniep H, Penzkofer T, Fiehler J, Hanning U, Dell'Orco A, Nawabi J. External Validation and Retraining of DeepBleed: The First Open-Source 3D Deep Learning Network for the Segmentation of Spontaneous Intracerebral and Intraventricular Hemorrhage.
venue_and_status: Journal of Clinical Medicine 12(12):4005; published; open access, methods and results checked
problem: External validity of an open-source haemorrhage segmentation network before and after retraining.
method: Multicentre retrospective validation of the original model (OM) and a retrained model (RM); Dice, sensitivity, PPV; pairwise Pearson correlations among ground-truth, OM and RM volumes; repeated-measures ANOVA; ICC for Dice agreement with raters.
data: 1040 patients with spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage.
main_result: Median Dice 0.84 (OM) vs 0.83 (RM); infratentorial Dice improved after retraining (p < 0.001); volume correlations r > 0.90 and no significant volume difference among GT, OM and RM; DeepBleed tended to underestimate volume.
relevance: Typical report of original-vs-retrained volume agreement by correlation at one timepoint (competitor check).
not_established: Correlation and ANOVA do not quantify agreement of change; no longitudinal or mixed-version analysis.

citation: Rahman MM, Berger D, Levman J. Novel Metrics for Evaluation and Validation of Regression-based Supervised Learning.
venue_and_status: 2022 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Computer Science and Data Engineering (CSDE), pp. 1-6; published; abstract only (IEEE paywall; thesis proposal blocked)
problem: Regression models retrained during validation make inconsistent sample-wise errors.
method: Regression error consistency (EC) metrics for sample-wise consistency of errors across repeatedly trained models (formula not read).
data: Six real-world datasets with six regressors; MNIST treated as regression with a CNN.
main_result: Random forest was accurate but less consistent in its error profiles (abstract).
relevance: A sample-level between-model consistency metric for continuous outputs, from in-lab validation rather than updates.
not_established: Definition not verified; repeated training, not deployed version updates; no longitudinal change.
code_or_data: Public-domain code stated in abstract (not checked)

citation: Jiang H, Narasimhan H, Bahri D, Cotter A, Rostamizadeh A. Churn Reduction via Distillation.
venue_and_status: ICLR 2022 per arXiv journal_ref and camera-ready header (OpenReview record not reachable); arXiv:2106.02654v2 read (definitions and evaluation)
problem: Retrained models should gain accuracy while keeping predictions close to the deployed base model.
method: Predictive churn = difference in predictions relative to a base model; ideal = fraction of disagreements; tractable soft churn = expected divergence d(g(x),h(x)) between output distributions; equivalence between distillation with the base model as teacher and training under an explicit churn constraint; evaluation with hard churn ('churn at cold accuracy').
data: Multiple datasets with fully connected, convolutional and transformer models.
main_result: Distillation performs strongly for low-churn training against recent baselines.
relevance: Supports the manuscript's distillation control: distilling from the old model is equivalent to constraining churn.
not_established: Classification outputs; no measurements or longitudinal change.

citation: Bhojanapalli S, Wilber MJ, Veit A, Rawat AS, Kim S, Menon AK, Kumar S. On the Reproducibility of Neural Network Predictions.
venue_and_status: arXiv preprint 2102.03349v1 (no venue in arXiv metadata); abstract
problem: Training randomness causes churn between independently trained networks.
method: Analysis of sources of churn (initialisation, mini-batch order, augmentation); minimum-entropy regularisers; co-distillation variant.
data: CIFAR and ImageNet.
main_result: Churn is substantial even for standard image classification; the proposed techniques reduce churn while improving accuracy (abstract).
relevance: Run-to-run prediction disagreement, a counterpart of the paper's training-run variability.
not_established: Classification; not deployed updates; venue not verified.

citation: Echterhoff JM, Faghri F, Vemulapalli R, Hu T-Y, Li C-L, Tuzel O, Pouransari H. MUSCLE: A Model Update Strategy for Compatible LLM Evolution.
venue_and_status: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2024, pp. 7320-7332; published; arXiv:2407.09435 read
problem: Updating LLM base models causes instance-level regressions in fine-tuned task adapters, including generative tasks scored on continuous metrics.
method: NFR_mc counts flips when both versions are wrong; smooth compatibility for a continuous similarity metric S: D(x_i)=S(M_v2(x_i),y_i)-S(M_v1(x_i),y_i); PFR~=(1/N) sum 1[D>0]; NFR~=(1/N) sum 1[D<0]; mean gain m_g and mean regression m_r=(1/(N*NFR~)) sum |D(x_i)|*1[D(x_i)<0]; compatibility adapter trained with masked distillation.
data: Llama 1->2, Vicuna and Phi updates; HellaSwag, PIQA, GSM8K, SAMSum.
main_result: Negative flips exceeded 60% in some update/task pairs; the compatibility adapter reduced NFR by up to 40% (Llama 1 to Llama 2).
relevance: Closest precedent for a compatibility metric on continuous per-instance scores (rate and magnitude of per-instance regression); directly adaptable to lesion-level change error.
not_established: Single timepoint; per-instance quality against a reference, not a between-version difference in a measured quantity; language tasks only.

citation: Matsuno R, Sakuma K. A Robust Backward Compatibility Metric for Model Retraining.
venue_and_status: Proceedings of the 32nd ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM 2023), pp. 4190-4194; published short paper; abstract
problem: Sample-based backward-compatibility metrics are sensitive to label noise.
method: Metric that scores whether the accuracy over each input's conditional distribution is at least as high as before; compatible retraining method; generalisation-error bound.
data: Not verified.
main_result: Metric and retraining method are robust to label noise with equal or better trade-offs (abstract).
relevance: Further primary definition in the classification compatibility family.
not_established: Classification only; definition not read.

citation: Matsuno R. Backward Compatibility in Attributive Explanation and Enhanced Model Training Method.
venue_and_status: ECAI 2024, Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence and Applications; published; abstract
problem: Model updates change the explanations attached to predictions.
method: BCX: average agreement between pre- and post-update attributive explanations among samples both models predict correctly; BCX-aware training (BCXR), including an L2-distance variant.
data: Eight real-world datasets (abstract).
main_result: BCXR gives better trade-offs between predictive performance and BCX (abstract).
relevance: Compatibility defined on continuous-valued outputs (attribution vectors) across versions.
not_established: Explanations, not measurements; conditioned on correct predictions; single timepoint; definition not read.

citation: Lopez-Paz D, Ranzato M. Gradient Episodic Memory for Continual Learning.
venue_and_status: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 30 (NIPS 2017); published (official PDF)
problem: Measuring and limiting forgetting when tasks are learned sequentially.
method: Accuracy matrix R (R_ij = test accuracy on task j after learning task i); ACC; backward transfer BWT = (1/(T-1)) sum_{i<T} (R_T,i - R_i,i); forward transfer FWT; GEM episodic-memory constraint.
data: MNIST permutations and rotations; CIFAR-100.
main_result: GEM limits negative backward transfer (forgetting) and allows positive backward transfer.
relevance: Primary definition of backward transfer, the continual-learning metric easily confused with backward compatibility; it measures performance retention, not agreement between versions.
not_established: Accuracy-based; no agreement or measurement comparison.

citation: Kumari P, Chauhan J, Bozorgpour A, Huang B, Azad R, Merhof D. Continual learning in medical image analysis: A comprehensive review of recent advancements and future prospects.
venue_and_status: Medical Image Analysis 106:103730; published review; abstract (arXiv 2312.17004 version exists)
problem: Overview of continual learning for medical image analysis.
method: Systematic review of scenarios, techniques (rehearsal, regularisation, architectural, hybrid), evaluation schemes and metrics.
data: Not applicable.
main_result: Continual learning is an emerging response to drifting medical data; evaluation centres on catastrophic forgetting and stability-plasticity (abstract).
relevance: Current survey for model updating in medical imaging.
not_established: Abstract only; no statement found on agreement of measurements across versions.

citation: Zhang J, Wen S, Du X, Jia X, Shi J, Du D, Li R, Shen B. Teacher-Referenced Heatmap Coverage for Auditing Attribution Shifts in Updated CT Classifiers.
venue_and_status: Journal of Imaging Informatics in Medicine, published online 22 Sep 2026 (no volume yet); abstract
problem: Model updates may change CT classifiers' attribution maps without changing predictive performance.
method: Grad-CAM maps of a baseline and a decision-distilled ResNet18 compared with a frozen model-derived reference using a heatmap coverage metric (missed circular coverage, nearest-peak distance); three CT cohorts; three seeds.
data: Three held-out CT cohorts (Priv-EGFR, Chest CT-Scan, RADGEN), slice level.
main_result: Thresholded IoU was often near zero; update effects on attribution endpoints were cohort- and seed-dependent; the endpoints measure internal consistency, not clinical correctness.
relevance: Only medical-imaging study found that audits output consistency across model versions with a dedicated metric (explanations of a classifier).
not_established: Classification explanations, not measurements; no longitudinal change.

citation: Hatherley J, Sparrow R. Diachronic and synchronic variation in the performance of adaptive machine learning systems: the ethical challenges.
venue_and_status: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association 30(2):361-366 (online 15 Nov 2022); published tutorial; open access, read in full
problem: Ethical issues raised by adaptive (continual-learning) medical ML systems.
method: Conceptual tutorial distinguishing diachronic evolution (change over time) from synchronic variation (between cotemporaneous sites).
data: Not applicable.
main_result: Diachronic evolution and synchronic variation challenge care quality, informed consent and equity; a system that differs from its previous iterations is hard for clinicians to trust.
relevance: Ethical framing of outputs that change across versions during a patient's care.
not_established: No empirical data or measurement analysis.

citation: Sculley D, Holt G, Golovin D, Davydov E, Phillips T, Ebner D, Chaudhary V, Young M, Crespo J-F, Dennison D. Hidden Technical Debt in Machine Learning Systems.
venue_and_status: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 28 (NIPS 2015); published (official PDF)
problem: ML-specific maintenance risks in production systems.
method: Position paper: entanglement and the CACE principle (Changing Anything Changes Everything), correction cascades, undeclared consumers, unstable data dependencies.
data: Not applicable.
main_result: Model outputs written to files or logs may be consumed silently by other systems; a silent update that corrects a previously mis-calibrated signal can have sudden ramifications for its consumers.
relevance: Software-engineering precedent for the mechanism: a stored old-version measurement is a consumer coupled to the old version's calibration.
not_established: Conceptual; no measurements or quantification.

citation: Hu W, Bansal R, Cao K, Rao N, Subbian K, Leskovec J. Learning Backward Compatible Embeddings.
venue_and_status: Proceedings of the 28th ACM SIGKDD Conference (KDD 2022), pp. 3018-3028; published; arXiv:2206.03040v1 read at methods level
problem: Updating an embedding model breaks consumer models trained on stored historical embedding versions.
method: Keep-latest framework with learned backward transformations that align version k to version k-1 and compose to any historical version; compared with Keep-All (keep every model version), Fix-0 (never update), fine-tuning and other variants; best variant BC-Aligner; compatibility judged by consumer-task degradation relative to Keep-All.
data: Real-world recommender-system application; three datasets; five unintended consumer tasks.
main_result: BC-Aligner maintains near-perfect backward compatibility for consumer tasks over multiple updates while intended-task performance stays close to an unconstrained model.
relevance: Structural analogue of the paper's strategies: one version per record (Keep-All), no update (Fix-0), reprocessing, and a learned version-to-version transformation (cross-calibration).
not_established: Embeddings for recommender tasks; compatibility measured by downstream performance, not measurement agreement; no paired timepoints.

citation: Balachandran VB. Pay Only for Disagreement: Certified No-Regression Verdicts for Model Updates with Matching Label-Complexity Bounds.
venue_and_status: arXiv preprint 2609.17560v1 (22 Jul 2026); not peer reviewed; abstract
problem: Certifying that an update (retraining, fine-tuning, quantisation, vendor swap) is not worse than its predecessor.
method: Paired risk-difference auditing built on a support identity (the risk difference lives on inputs where the two models disagree); two-tier sequential protocol with a zero-label tier and anytime-valid confidence sequences on sampled disagreements; machine-checkable evidence records.
data: 14,000+ replayed audit streams over 785 update pairs, including LoRA fine-tunes of language models up to 1.4B parameters.
main_result: Miscoverage 0.0002 at nominal 5%, power 0.986, and 56% of benign updates certified with zero labels (abstract).
relevance: Acceptance-test framing for updates based on paired disagreement, conceptually parallel to the paper's identity that the change-error difference equals the between-version baseline difference.
not_established: Preprint; classification and LLM outputs; no continuous measurement or change over time.

citation: Ötleş E, Denton BT, Wiens J. Updating Clinical Risk Stratification Models Using Rank-Based Compatibility: Approaches for Evaluating and Optimizing Clinician-Model Team Performance.
venue_and_status: Proceedings of the 8th Machine Learning for Healthcare Conference, PMLR 219:529-547; published; arXiv:2308.05619 and PMLR PDF read
problem: Threshold-based compatibility (BTC) does not suit models that rank patients by continuous risk.
method: Rank-based compatibility C^R(f_o,f_u) = sum_{i in I0} sum_{j in I1} 1(p_i^o < p_j^o)*1(p_i^u < p_j^u) / sum_{i in I0} sum_{j in I1} 1(p_i^o < p_j^o) (Eq. 3); general form for any ordered labels, e.g. integer or real values (Appendix Eq. 6); AUROC-based bounds; differentiable rank-incompatibility loss.
data: MIMIC-III in-hospital mortality; 150 standard updates per original model; 40 replications.
main_result: Adding the rank-incompatibility loss raised C^R by 0.019 (95% CI 0.005 to 0.035) with AUROC change -0.009 (-0.030 to 0.011); standard updates rarely reach very high C^R.
relevance: An existing compatibility metric for continuous outputs in clinical AI; the revision must cite and distinguish it.
not_established: Rank-based, so invariant to monotone calibration shifts between versions (the shift that drives the paper's retention cost); single timepoint; binary-outcome case study only.

citation: Riley RD, Collins GS. Stability of clinical prediction models developed using statistical or machine learning methods.
venue_and_status: Biometrical Journal 65(8):2200302; published; open access, read in part (PMC10952221)
problem: Small development datasets make individual risk predictions unstable across plausible re-developed models.
method: Four levels of stability; repeat model building in bootstrap samples (e.g., 1000 models); prediction instability plot; individual MAPE_i = sum_b |p_bi - p_i| / B and average MAPE over individuals; calibration, classification and decision-curve instability plots.
data: Simulations and clinical case studies (e.g., 27 candidate predictors; unpenalised logistic regression vs LASSO).
main_result: Individual-level instability is often considerable (case study: average MAPE 0.038 when forcing all 27 predictors vs 0.029 with LASSO) and manifests as miscalibration in new data; the average MAPE masks individual differences.
relevance: Clinical-statistics precedent for an individual-level absolute-difference summary between two models' continuous outputs (cf. the lesion-level between-version baseline difference).
not_established: Bootstrap re-development, not deployed version updates; estimated risks, not physical measurements; no change over time.

citation: Yusufujiang M, Andaur Navarro CL, Damen JAA, Takada T, Geersing G-J, Hooft L, Schuit E, Moons KGM, de Jong VMT, van Smeden M. Prediction models developed using artificial intelligence: similar predictive performances with highly varying predictions for individuals - an illustration in deep vein thrombosis.
venue_and_status: Diagnostic and Prognostic Research 10:1; published; abstract
problem: Do models with similar discrimination give similar individual risk estimates?
method: Five modelling techniques (unpenalised and ridge logistic regression, random forest, SVM, neural network) on fixed predictors; discrimination, calibration and individual-prediction stability.
data: 6087 patients with suspected DVT (1146 with DVT).
main_result: Three models had AUC about 0.84 yet individual DVT probabilities varied substantially; random forest overestimated and SVM underestimated risks; classifications near thresholds differed.
relevance: Similar aggregate performance does not imply individual-level agreement (analogue of a Dice gain without measurement compatibility).
not_established: Different techniques, not version updates; no measurements.

citation: Correia C, Ferreira AEA, Martins L, Bento MP, Guerreiro S, Pereira RR, Gomes AS, Bono J, Ferreira H, Bizarro P. MUSE: Multi-Tenant Model Serving With Seamless Model Updates.
venue_and_status: arXiv preprint 2602.11776v1 (12 Feb 2026), comment 'under review for KDD 2026 ADS'; no published record found in Crossref; abstract
problem: Retraining shifts score distributions and invalidates client-managed decision thresholds.
method: Serving framework with intent-based routing and a two-level score transformation that maps model outputs to a stable reference distribution.
data: Production fraud-detection deployment (Feedzai), over 55 billion events in 12 months (abstract).
main_result: Model lead time reduced from weeks to minutes while thresholds stay valid (abstract).
relevance: Industrial precedent for cross-calibrating continuous outputs between versions by distribution mapping, analogous to the paper's scalar recalibration.
not_established: Distribution-level mapping cannot correct instance-level disagreement; preprint; fraud scores, not measurements.

citation: D'Amour A, Heller K, Moldovan D, Adlam B, Alipanahi B, Beutel A, et al. Underspecification Presents Challenges for Credibility in Modern Machine Learning.
venue_and_status: Journal of Machine Learning Research 23(226):1-61; published; abstract (official JMLR page)
problem: Pipelines can return many predictors with equivalently strong held-out performance that behave differently in deployment.
method: Concept of underspecification with examples from computer vision, medical imaging, NLP, EHR-based clinical risk prediction and medical genomics.
data: Multiple domains (abstract).
main_result: Predictors treated as equivalent on held-out data can behave very differently in deployment, causing instability (abstract).
relevance: Context for the wide training-run spread of the between-version shift despite consistent overlap gains.
not_established: Not about sequential updates or measurement compatibility; abstract level.

citation: Spiliotis E, Petropoulos F. On the update frequency of univariate forecasting models.
venue_and_status: European Journal of Operational Research 314(1):111-121 (online 2023); published; abstract
problem: Is it necessary to update forecasting models at every review period?
method: Updating scenarios from full re-specification and re-estimation to no updating; conventional and machine-learning models.
data: Two large datasets of monthly and daily series.
main_result: Intermediate updating gives similar or better accuracy at lower cost; frequent updates can add forecast instability.
relevance: Neighbouring field (forecasting) treating changes of continuous outputs caused by re-estimation as instability.
not_established: Forecasts, not measurements; no mixed-version comparison.

citation: González C, Ranem A, Pinto dos Santos D, Othman A, Mukhopadhyay A. Lifelong nnU-Net: a framework for standardized medical continual learning.
venue_and_status: Scientific Reports 13:9381; published; open access, read in part (PMC10256748)
problem: Standardised evaluation of sequentially updated (continual) medical segmentation models.
method: nnU-Net-based framework; five continual-learning methods; Dice, backward transfer (forgetting) and forward transfer.
data: Public prostate, hippocampus and cardiac segmentation datasets.
main_result: No explored method consistently achieved positive backward transfer; rehearsal-based methods forgot least.
relevance: Shows how sequential updates of medical segmenters are evaluated: overlap retention (Dice, BWT), not agreement of measured volumes.
not_established: No volume, measurement-agreement or longitudinal analysis.
code_or_data: Code and trained models released (as stated by the authors; not checked)

citation: Su T-L, Jaki T, Hickey GL, Buchan I, Sperrin M. A review of statistical updating methods for clinical prediction models.
venue_and_status: Statistical Methods in Medical Research 27(1):185-197 (online 2016); published; abstract
problem: How to update existing clinical prediction models instead of developing new ones.
method: Review of simple coefficient updating (recalibration), meta-models and dynamic updating; empirical comparison.
data: UK cardiac surgery mortality data.
main_result: No single updating strategy performed well enough to be used exclusively; models commonly become miscalibrated over time.
relevance: Statistical lineage of recalibration as model updating (cf. scalar cross-calibration maps).
not_established: Outcome prediction models, not measurement instruments; no version-compatibility metric.

citation: Watson-Daniels J, Parkes DC, Ustun B. Predictive Multiplicity in Probabilistic Classification.
venue_and_status: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence 37(9):10306-10314; published; abstract
problem: How much do risk estimates vary across near-optimal competing models?
method: Measures of variation in risk estimates over the set of competing models; optimisation-based computation for convex empirical risk minimisation.
data: Real-world risk-assessment datasets (abstract).
main_result: Predictive multiplicity in risk estimates is common and relates to dataset characteristics (abstract).
relevance: Continuous-output disagreement among equally good models, a neighbour of version compatibility.
not_established: Not sequential updates; not measurements.

citation: Ying C, Chen Y, Yan Y, Flores S, Laforest R, Benzinger TLS, An H. Accuracy and Longitudinal Consistency of PET/MR Attenuation Correction in Amyloid PET Imaging amid Software and Hardware Upgrades.
venue_and_status: American Journal of Neuroradiology 46(3):635-642 (online 9 Sep 2024); published; abstract (full text not retrievable)
problem: Scanner software and head-coil upgrades during multi-year longitudinal amyloid PET/MR studies.
method: Deep-learning Dixon attenuation correction fine-tuned by transfer learning for two scanner software versions and two head coils; accuracy against CT attenuation correction; longitudinal consistency (within-subject CV, ICC) and power analysis.
data: 329 participants; 38 scanned twice within about 3 years.
main_result: High accuracy regardless of software version or coil (median cortical PET mean relative absolute error about 1.0-1.2%); within-subject CV and ICC of SUVR comparable to CT attenuation correction; similar sample sizes needed to detect change.
relevance: Closest medical-imaging study of longitudinal consistency of a deep-learning quantitative pipeline amid version upgrades (overlaps T2).
not_established: The upgrades were to the scanner, with the network re-tuned per configuration; no comparison of stored old-version values with reprocessing is reported in the abstract.

citation: Oya A, Nakayama M, Uno T, Ueda H, Yoshida I, Fujiya A, Nomura Y, Okizaki A. Comparison of the diagnostic accuracy of VSBONE BSI versions for detecting bone metastases in breast and prostate carcinoma patients using conventional and CZT detector gamma cameras.
venue_and_status: Annals of Nuclear Medicine 39(5):466-475; published; abstract
problem: Do upgrades of an automated bone scan index (BSI) software improve diagnostic accuracy?
method: Three versions of VSBONE BSI on bone scintigraphy from conventional and CZT gamma cameras; ROC analysis against metastasis status.
data: 287 patients with breast or prostate carcinoma.
main_result: AUC increased with version upgrades; in metastasis-negative patients BSI values decreased with each upgrade.
relevance: A quantitative AI output shifting systematically between versions while accuracy improves (overlaps T2).
not_established: Cross-sectional; no longitudinal BSI change across versions.

citation: Zhang B, Ge Y, Shen Y, Li Y, Yuan C, Xu X, Wang Y, Shan Y. Hot-Refresh Model Upgrades with Regression-Free Compatible Training in Image Retrieval.
venue_and_status: ICLR 2022 poster (official conference page; OpenReview forum HTp-6yLGGX); arXiv:2201.09724v1 abstract read (arXiv title says 'Regression-Alleviating')
problem: If a new retrieval model is deployed before the gallery is fully backfilled, new-to-old and new-to-new comparisons coexist and cause regressions.
method: Regression-alleviating compatible training (new-to-old positive pairs pushed to be more similar than new-to-old and new-to-new negative pairs); uncertainty-based backfilling order.
data: Large-scale retrieval benchmarks such as Google Landmark.
main_result: Reduces model regression (negative flips) during on-the-fly backfilling (abstract).
relevance: Retrieval analogue of a partly reprocessed record: mixing outputs of two versions in one comparison causes regression.
not_established: Embeddings and retrieval accuracy; no measurements or change over time.

citation: Hatherley JJ. A moving target in AI-assisted decision-making: dataset shift, model updating, and the problem of update opacity.
venue_and_status: Ethics and Information Technology 27(2):20; published; abstract
problem: How model updating affects ML-assisted decision-making itself.
method: Philosophical analysis introducing 'update opacity' (users cannot understand how or why an update changed a system's reasoning or behaviour); discusses bi-factual explanations, dynamic model reporting and update compatibility as responses.
data: Not applicable.
main_result: Update opacity raises distinctive epistemic and safety concerns that existing black-box remedies are ill-equipped to address; each proposed strategy has limitations (abstract).
relevance: Supports recording the model version behind each stored output and reporting updates (the paper's third practice step).
not_established: No empirical data; not about measurements.

citation: Mohanty V, Lim J, Luther K. What Lies Beneath? Exploring the Impact of Underlying AI Model Updates in AI-Infused Systems.
venue_and_status: Proceedings of the 2025 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems, pp. 1-21; published; abstract
problem: Can users notice silent or minimally communicated AI model updates, and how do these affect their behaviour?
method: Online experiment on detecting model updates and a diary study in a real deployment of facial recognition for historical photo identification.
data: Online experiment participants and diary-study users (numbers not checked).
main_result: Users struggle to notice model updates; updates change downstream behaviour and performance and lead to divergent folk theories (abstract).
relevance: Evidence that silent vendor updates go unnoticed, supporting version recording for stored measurements.
not_established: Not medical; no measurements.
